item.message: Skill descriptions were shortened to fit the 2% skills context budget. Codex can still see every skill, but some descriptions are shorter. Disable unused skills or plugins to leave more room for the rest.

item.text: {"brief_complete":false,"completion_reason":"Three material workflow-experience decisions remain about operator attention, explicit context sharing, and recovery ownership.","questions":[{"decision_key":"runs_attention_inbox_default","label":"Runs landing view","context":"The new Runs tab will replace the current Review surface and own execution evidence, validation, and approvals. An attention inbox means a filtered list of runs that currently require an operator decision or recovery.","evidence":"`apps/web/app/page.jsx` currently exposes Review rather than Runs, while `packages/contracts/index.mjs` defines `approval_required`, failed, canceled, and completed states that the new Runs surface must present.","impact":"Approvals and failures must be noticed quickly without burying completed evidence.","question":"What should operators see first in Runs?","choices":[{"number":1,"text":"Action inbox","consequence":"Show approvals, failures, and blocked runs first, with recent completed runs one click away; this optimizes daily operations but requires clear empty and resolved states."},{"number":2,"text":"Recent activity","consequence":"Show every run in time order; this is easy to understand but urgent decisions can disappear in a busy deployment."},{"number":3,"text":"Saved personal view","consequence":"Open each operator’s last-used filters; this supports specialized workflows but makes the default experience less predictable across collaborators."}],"allow_multiple":false,"recommended_choice":1,"recommendation_reason":"The recorded human-controlled final gate makes pending decisions the most important daily work.","priority":95},{"decision_key":"new_conversation_context_attachment","label":"Prior context","context":"Work memory is isolated per conversation. Prior context means selected messages, artifacts, or validated records from another conversation that the operator deliberately brings into a new one.","evidence":"`packages/contracts/index.mjs` defines the per-run context contract, and `services/nexus-node/src/run-coordinator.mjs` routes submissions through canonical run records rather than relying on hidden model history.","impact":"New work must reuse useful knowledge without silently leaking unrelated conversation history.","question":"How should prior context enter a new conversation?","choices":[{"number":1,"text":"Explicit context attachments","consequence":"Let the operator select conversations, artifacts, or validated records before sending; this preserves isolation and provenance but adds a deliberate setup step."},{"number":2,"text":"Automatic recent context","consequence":"Attach recent related work based on routing signals; this feels faster but can introduce surprising or irrelevant information."},{"number":3,"text":"Shared project context","consequence":"Give every conversation in a chosen project the same background; this simplifies continuity but weakens conversation-level isolation over time."}],"allow_multiple":false,"recommended_choice":1,"recommendation_reason":"Explicit attachment preserves the recorded per-conversation boundary while still enabling intentional reuse.","priority":92},{"decision_key":"paused_workflow_recovery_surface","label":"Recovery home","context":"A paused workflow is an accepted execution that cannot continue until an operator retries, changes an allowed input, approves a gate, or ends it. The choice decides which tab owns those recovery actions.","evidence":"`kits/jobs-kit/index.mjs` owns durable retry, cancellation, timeout, progress, and terminal state; `packages/contracts/index.mjs` defines run states; and the six-tab decision assigns workflow definitions to Workflows but execution evidence and approvals to Runs.","impact":"Operators must recover blocked work from one predictable place without mixing execution controls into workflow design.","question":"Where should operators recover a paused workflow?","choices":[{"number":1,"text":"Runs recovery panel","consequence":"Put retry, approve, cancel, and failure details beside the immutable run record, while Workflows links there; this keeps one operational authority but adds a navigation step from the workflow definition."},{"number":2,"text":"Workflow instance panel","consequence":"Recover executions within Workflows beside their schedule and stages; this feels contextual but mixes mutable design with immutable run operations."},{"number":3,"text":"Controls in both tabs","consequence":"Expose synchronized recovery controls in Runs and Workflows; this reduces navigation but creates duplicate surfaces that must remain perfectly consistent."}],"allow_multiple":false,"recommended_choice":1,"recommendation_reason":"It follows the recorded six-tab ownership by keeping execution decisions with their canonical evidence.","priority":89}]}
